title: See how the units and teams fit together
description: A tree draws each part as a node under the part it belongs to, so the structure reads from left to right.
version: 0.0.1
styles: [scientific]

## Three units, eleven teams

These illustrative figures give the headcount of each team. A unit that has teams under it carries no figure of its own; the chart never invents one.

```chart
type: tree
title: Engineering has the most teams
subtitle: Each node is a part; colour is the top-level unit
data:
  inline:
    - {unit: Engineering}
    - {unit: Platform, reports_to: Engineering}
    - {unit: Core, reports_to: Platform, headcount: 8}
    - {unit: Tooling, reports_to: Platform, headcount: 6}
    - {unit: Product, reports_to: Engineering, headcount: 22}
    - {unit: Data, reports_to: Engineering, headcount: 9}
    - {unit: Sales}
    - {unit: EMEA, reports_to: Sales, headcount: 12}
    - {unit: Americas, reports_to: Sales, headcount: 16}
    - {unit: Operations}
    - {unit: People, reports_to: Operations, headcount: 5}
    - {unit: Finance, reports_to: Operations, headcount: 4}
encoding: {label: unit, parent: reports_to, y: headcount}
```

*Source: Illustrative values.*

Use the keyboard or pointer to read each part's path, its headcount where given and how many parts sit under it.
